title: TidalWorks inference savings heuristic analysis
summary: Heuristic-driven before/after cost model for TidalWorks (customer). Focused on reducing token and GPU-unit spend by combining lightweight quantization, targeted batching, prefix caching and model routing to cheaper variants for non-critical requests. This sheet captures baseline metrics, optimized scenario assumptions, per-component delta, sensitivity grid and a conservative rollout plan.
baseline_metrics: Baseline measured (30-day window ending 2025-01-31): 1.2B input tokens / month, 0.3B generated tokens / month, average request latency 420ms (p95 720ms), median tokens per request 120, peak qps 75, daily GPU hours (A100 equivalent) 110 hrs, hosted cost $46,800/month (compute + infra + model licensing). Primary model: open-llama-large-2 (39B) with FP16, no quantization, minimal batching (avg 1.2 requests/batch), KV cache disabled for short-lived sessions, embeddings handled by dedicated small CPU instance (minor cost). Current QA/accuracy metrics: intent F1 0.92, summary ROUGE-L 0.67.
optimized_metrics: Optimized scenario (conservative defaults): apply dynamic batching to reach 2.6 requests/batch average, enable 4-bit quantization on serving path for non-candidates, enable prefix KV cache with expected hit-rate 28% (session reuse patterns), route low-confidence reranking to a 7B cheap variant, move embeddings to vector-search-side computed asynchronously to reduce synchronous compute. Projected monthly tokens served same, effective GPU hours drop to 64 hrs/day equivalent (monthly ~48% reduction), projected hosted cost $27,300/month. Latency impact: mean latency ~480ms (+60ms avg) but p95 remains within SLA using canary fallback to larger instance for tail. Expected QA delta: intent F1 -0.008 (0.8% drop) on producer text, reranking unaffected.
assumptions: 1) Quantization to 4-bit yields 1.9x throughput improvement on existing kernels without retraining; 2) Batching benefit scales linearly until 3x under current CPU/GPU stacking; 3) KV cache hit-rate estimated from session study (sample size 1200 sessions) and will vary by product usage; 4) Routing rules correctly classify ~86% of low-cost candidates via confidence threshold; 5) No additional infra egress or S3 costs beyond minor storage for cache metadata. If any assumption fails, savings drop proportionally (see sensitivity grid).
recommended_changes:
- Enable workload-aware batching with 50ms window and async flush for tail traffic.
- Deploy quantized 4-bit serving path for model variants; keep FP16 path for quality-sensitive routes.
- Turn on prefix/KV caching for authenticated sessions and increase cache TTL to 30m for repeated queries.
- Add routing policy: confidence < 0.65 -> route to 7B reranker, confidence >= 0.65 -> 39B quantized path.
- Offload synchronous embedding generation: compute embeddings in background worker and cache vector ids to reduce blocking cost.
- Implement incremental validation eval on 5% of traffic to monitor quality regressions and metric drift.
- Add cost tagging and per-route telemetry to attribute savings to product features.
estimated_savings: Conservative: 30% month-1 net reduction ($13,900/mo). Expected steady-state: 41% net reduction ($19,200/mo) after tuning and cache warmup. Breakdown: quantization + model routing 24% of savings, batching 9%, KV caching 6%, embedding offload 2%. Upside scenario (all assumptions hold and 40% cache hit): up to 52% reduction. Downside (quantization perf not achieved): as low as 12% reduction.
cost_model_spreadsheet: Spreadsheet tab names: baseline_input, optimized_scenario, per_component_delta, sensitivity_grid, rollout_costs. Key parameters exposed: token price ($/1M tokens), GPU-hour price (A100 equiv), batch_window_ms, kv_cache_hit, quant_gain_factor. Link: drive:/product/optimize/spreadsheets/tidalworks-cost-model-2025q1 (internal sheet).
sensitivity_notes: Most sensitive levers: quant_gain_factor and kv_cache_hit. If quant_gain_factor < 1.4x throughput, savings drop >15%. If kv_cache_hit < 12%, caching yields negligible savings. Batching parameters sensitive to tail-latency constraints; increasing batch window beyond 80ms creates customer-facing latency degradation. See sensitivity_grid tab for tornado chart.
rollout_plan: 1) Lab validation (1 week): benchmark quantized kernels on representative inputs, confirm QA delta <1%. 2) Canary (2% traffic, 2 weeks): monitor cost, latency, QA metrics. 3) Gradual ramp (2% -> 10% -> 30% -> 100%) over 6 weeks with automatic rollback triggers: delta intent F1 >= -0.02 OR p95 latency increase >200ms. 4) Post-rollout: stabilize caches, tune routing thresholds, and run weekly evals for 8 weeks. Responsible: Miguel Ortega (eng), Samira Patel (product).
open_questions:
- Does TidalWorks have regulatory constraints on model quantization for financial summaries?
- Can product team accept a small uptick in avg latency for 40% cost savings?
- Is there appetite to invest in re-training a distilled 7B variant vs using open 7B?
- Are there pre-existing quotas or reserved capacity agreements that change unit pricing?
- Who will own long-term cache eviction strategy for compliance?
